digital-culture.dwp_take: Most organizations have figured out how to handle employees who are sick or burned out, but they completely ghost them the moment they try to come back to work. digital-culture.title: The end of the ‘good enough’ worker
digital-culture.excerpt: I watch about a thousand companies make hiring decisions in real time as the CEO of Paraform, the world’s largest recruiting marketplace. The pattern I’ve seen over the last 18 months is so consistent
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are raising their hiring bar dramatically, no longer settling for average performers because AI now handles routine work that used to pad mediocre resumes. This matters to digital workplace pros because it fundamentally changes how you need to position skills, design onboarding, and manage performance for a workforce that needs to demonstrate real value from day one. The irony is that after decades of participation trophy culture, we're finally getting back to the radical idea that people should be good at their jobs, though I suspect the transition will be painful for everyone who coasted.

digital-culture.title: Companies Keep Slashing Employees’ Benefits for the Worst Reasons
digital-culture.excerpt: Workers are getting worse health care, parental leave, and retirement benefits, showing once and for all that your job doesn’t love you back.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are cutting employee benefits across health care, parental leave, and retirement packages, often with weak justifications that amount to little more than "we can get away with it." Here's the reality: if your org is slashing benefits to pad executive bonuses while claiming budget constraints, don't be shocked when your best people start job hunting and your employer brand turns into a punchline.
